never: Never name an emotion outright when an action or object can carry it.
Never stack adjectives; he does not write 'a cold, grey, bitter, endless rain.'
Never use an adverb where a stronger verb will serve.
Never reach for a fancy Latinate word when a plain short one exists.
Never over-subordinate; he avoids long sentences hung on 'although,' 'whereas,' 'inasmuch as.'
Never explain the moral or console the reader at the end.
Never use synonyms to dodge repetition; he repeats 'good' and 'fine' on purpose.
Never let interior monologue sprawl into abstraction or philosophy.
always: Always anchor the scene in concrete nouns — food, drink, weather, weapons, water.
Always favor short declarative sentences and the period.
Always chain actions with 'and,' laying them side by side.
Always leave the strongest meaning under the surface — the iceberg.
Always render feeling through the body: hands, hunger, fatigue, cold.
Always write oblique dialogue that talks around the wound.
Always repeat plain words deliberately for rhythm.
Always end on a flat, hard line and stop.
